items.problem: Unqualified references to a source helper type whose name equals the WinUI 3 project's root namespace fail (CS0234), and the natural using-alias fix fails too (CS0576); the XAML compiler then cascades (WMC1509 -> WMC0909/WMC1111). The dev-agent lost ~3 build cycles guessing the fix.
items.evidence: session-log 4116-4118 (CS0234 '...does not exist in the namespace LinguisticServices'), 4343-4345 (CS0576 alias conflict), 4508-4523 (final fix 'using static Sample.LinguisticServices;'); XAML cascade 4126/4353. lessons.json errors_encountered + dev_agent_struggles.
items.root_cause: Project scaffolded with the sample's name -> root namespace == a source helper type name (Sample.LinguisticServices). Bare identifier binds to the namespace, not the class; aliasing to that name is illegal.
items.change: Added a new subsection to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Common build errors after the namespace rewrite': 'CS0234 (a handful) / CS0576 — the project name collides with a source type or namespace'. Explains the collision, warns against the using-alias trap (CS0576), gives two deterministic fixes (using static / global:: qualification), and notes the XAML WMC1509->WMC0909/WMC1111 cascade clears once C# compiles.
items.expected_effect: On a re-run, an agent hitting CS0234 '...in the namespace <ProjectName>' or CS0576 recognises the root-namespace/type collision immediately and applies global::/using static in one edit instead of trying an illegal alias.
items.falsifiable_check: Re-run a sample whose feature class name equals the project name: the collision is resolved in a single edit (no CS0576 detour), and MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md now contains a 'CS0576' entry (previously absent).

deferred_to_human: Tier-0/harness option: have the scaffold set the WinUI 3 project <RootNamespace> to the source's code-behind namespace (e.g. SDKTemplate) instead of the sample name, which would prevent the root-namespace/type collision at its source. Not auto-applied because project naming is owned by the scaffold/driver, not the winui-uwp-migration skill.
